messages.subject: This function works on the command line...
parts:
Folks,
The following function works if I repeat each statement on the
command line.

I successfully create an "inset" graph within a graph using the
viewport commands and following the example of the ggplot2 book
section 8.4.2

When I call it as a function I only get the inset graph. I am sure
that there must be something that I am missing regarding the way pdf()
or par() works in a function.

Thanks for your time,
KW

Here is my code:

pAndLgraph<-function(cf.data, upFront) {
# Create p and l in millions
pl<-pAndL(cf.data, upFront)/1000
names(pl)<-c("P.And.L")
# This is all the p and l less than the maximum value. I.e. the tail
pl.tail<-as.data.frame(pl[var1.pl<max(var1.pl)])
names(pl.tail)<-c("P.And.L")

pl.plot<-qplot(P.And.L, data = pl, geom = "density", size = I(.75))
pl.tail.plot<-qplot(P.And.L, data = pl.tail, geom = "density")
pl.tail.plot<-pl.tail.plot + theme_gray(9) + labs(x = NULL, y =
NULL) +
opts(plot.margin = unit(rep(0,4), "lines"))

pdf(file.choose(), width = 4, height = 4)
vp2<-viewport(width = .4, height = .4, x = .3, y = .7)
pl.plot
print(pl.tail.plot, vp = vp2)
dev.off()
}

messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: Re: This function works on the command line...
parts:
In a function you need to print all ggplot objects; in particular, you
need to print(pl.plot) for it to appear in the file.

HTH,

baptiste

parts:
On 21 March 2012 08:26, Brandon Hurr <brando...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Just out of curiosity, why is that the case?

ggplot2 and lattice produce plots using grid graphics, where one can
separate the production of grobs (GRaphical OBjects) that can be
stored as a description of the plot, and the actual drawing where
these grobs are pushed onto the device. With raw grid objects this is
the distinction between,

g = grid::rectGrob() # create a rectangle, draw nothing
grid::grid.draw(g) # draw it

ggplot2 and lattice work at a higher level, and define a print()
method to display the graphics description containing many grobs and
viewports. In the interactive read-eval-print R session, objects are
printed when their name is invoked on the command line. This is not
the case within a function, or in non-interactive mode, hence the need
to explicitely call print().

HTH,

b.

messages.subject: Re: This function works on the command line...
parts:
With the latest version of ggplot2, you can add inset plots as part of
the plot itself

?annotation_custom

which, among other things, allows you to use ggsave() to conveniently
save the two plots at once.

b.
